verdict: OK to lend in Ichalkaranji cotton spinning and yarn, but only to spinners with captive processing or diversified buyers and tight monthly stock-and-receivable discipline; avoid pure greige weavers and single-buyer converters until the loom shutdown and the stuck-stock problem clear.
title: Ichalkaranji cotton spinning & yarn: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
**A spinning unit buys cotton, converts it into yarn, and sells to weavers, knitters and traders; cash is made on the spread between cotton cost and yarn realisation, not on volume.** Ichalkaranji is India's largest greige fabric cluster at about 4,296 million metres a year [3], so the yarn demand here is derived demand from the loom floor. When the looms stop, yarn offtake stops with them. **That is exactly what has happened: about 15,000 airjet looms now run a 24-hour weekly shutdown to cut losses from the textile slowdown [1].** So when a proposal lands, check how much of the borrower's yarn goes to Ichalkaranji looms versus outside buyers; if it is mostly local loom supply, ask what share of capacity the buyer has idled. ## What the peers say
**Large spinners are doing well on yarn realisation: Nitin Spinners reported its highest-ever quarterly revenue of Rs 875 crore, up 10.3% YoY, with EBITDA margin at 17.78%, up 376 basis points YoY [4].** Sportking's Q1FY26 revenue fell 7.6% YoY to Rs 585.8 crore but EBITDA margin improved 40 basis points to 12.0%, with exports about 58% of revenue and up about 18% YoY [5]. **The lesson is that export-linked and integrated spinners are holding margin while local greige-only players absorb the shock.** Note the Sportking result is from Q1FY26, older than the Nitin Q1FY2027 call [4][5]. Rating methodology is clear that weaving is fixed-capital and working-capital intensive, and that leverage and receivable stretch drive vulnerability in a downturn [8][9][10]. ## How to grow safely
**Pursue spinners with captive processing or a finishing tie-up, exporters with a diversified buyer base, and units moving into MMF and blends [3].** Avoid stand-alone greige weavers and single-buyer converters exposed to the Rajasthan processing shutdown [2]. Structure working capital against stock and receivables with a monthly stock statement and a drawing-power linked to ageing; take the buyer-wise sales register every month, and a quarterly CMA. **Maharashtra GST collections are running 8.6% Apr-to-date versus India's 6.1% [D], and India-wide IIP for NIC 13 is up 13.1% YoY with bank credit up 15.2% against output up 11.9% [D] — the credit gap means discipline matters more than appetite.**

## Early-warning signs
**Watch the weekly loom shutdown extending beyond one day, receivable days crossing the borrower's own six-month average, and any shift of sales to cash-and-carry buyers.** If the borrower's yarn despatch to Ichalkaranji falls for two straight months, cut drawing power before the quarter closes.
